theater: 諾里西姆谷地與北意大利戰線

battle.name: 辛布里戰爭
battle.theater: 諾里西姆谷地與北意大利戰線
battle.brief: 前113年辛布里人自北方湧入阿爾卑斯，在諾里西姆谷地重創羅馬執政官軍，戰火自高盧燒到北意大利，前101年才以維爾凱萊的殘滅收場。卡面的科林斯青銅盔並非戰場實物，它早於本役數百年退出希臘軍備；對照物是辛布里人與羅馬步兵同樣戴的青銅頭盔，以及雙方都只能靠隊形站住的那道防線。

kit.name: 科林斯青銅盔
kit.history: 全正面開眼的青銅盔。看得見的代價是：戴它的人只能靠隊形活。

countries: 辛布里戰爭（前113年—前101年）是羅馬共和國與自北方遷徙下來的日耳曼部族聯盟之間的一場長戰，戰場從諾里西姆一路延伸到波河下游、比斯開灣北岸，最後打到西西里島。開戰的一方是辛布里人：這是一個由多個氏族拼成的部族聯盟，核心是辛布里本部，旁邊有同行的條頓人、阿姆布里昂人，以及在高盧北邊加入的條古里尼人與波伊人。他們的戰鬥單位是「王」率領的部落聯軍，沒有常備兵員與固定國界，糧食靠隨軍牛群與車隊維持。另一方是羅馬共和國：兩位執政官分別領兵，核心是公民兵團與拉丁同盟的盟軍，輔兵由高盧盟邦與希臘殖民地馬薩利亞提供騎兵，羅得島提供標槍投擲手中隊。真正的第三方是整個高盧部落世界：阿洛布羅吉人、阿維爾尼人、艾杜伊人、塞格納尼人先被辛布里打崩，再向羅馬求援；塞比那、馬爾西利亞一類的城市在戰事中被劫。最後階段波伊人與因蘇布列人倒向辛布里，利古里人與他們合流，戰線因此延伸到底里亞與利古里亞海岸。
countriesEn: The Cimbrian War (113–101 BC) was a long conflict between the Roman Republic and a confederation of northern Germanic peoples who had migrated southward, fought across a theatre that stretched from Noricum down the Po valley to the north coast of the Bay of Biscay, and finally into Sicily. One side was the Cimbri, a tribal confederation assembled from several clans, centred on the Cimbri proper and accompanied by the Teutones and the Ambrones, and later joined in northern Gaul by the Tigurini and the Boii. Their fighting force was a tribal levy led by a king, with no standing army and no fixed frontier, and food travelled with the army in herds of cattle and wagon trains. The other side was the Roman Republic: two consuls each commanded a wing, the core being the citizen legions together with the contingents of the Latin League, auxiliaries supplied with cavalry by the Gallic allies and by the Greek colony of Massalia, and a cohort of javelin-throwers provided by Rhodes. The third party was the Gaulish tribal world itself: the Allobroges, Arverni, Aedui and Sequani were broken by the Cimbri and then appealed to Rome for help, while towns such as Taurentia were plundered as the war rolled past them. In the final phase the Boii and Insubres turned to the Cimbri, the Ligurians joined them, and the war reached the Po valley and the Ligurian coast.
people: 羅馬方面的關鍵人物幾乎全在執政官與將軍之間。前113年出任執政官的加尼亞斯·帕皮里烏斯·馬斯科率主力沿阿爾卑斯東麓南下，遇辛布里大軍而潰，是羅馬共和國在這場戰爭裡第一次敗在北方部族手上；同行的普布利烏斯·科爾涅利烏斯·阿西納在撤退中陣亡。真正改變戰局的是蓋烏斯·馬略，他在前107年至前101年間五次擔任執政官，前104年取得「辛布里征服者」的封號，是唯一從頭打到尾的人。他重整了步兵中隊的編制、標槍與短劍的配合、營壘紀律與騎兵指揮，並把羅得島、馬薩利亞的雇傭兵與高盧盟軍編入作戰序列。前105年阿奎·塞克斯提亞之戰以伏兵側擊全殲條頓人；前104年起再以底里亞的長期圍城消耗辛布里人。他的同僚與屬將包括馬爾庫斯·尤尼烏斯·西拉努斯（前109年塔高之役慘敗）、昆圖斯·塞爾維利烏斯·凱皮奧與蓋烏斯·弗拉維烏斯·芬布里亞（前105年阿勞西奧全軍覆沒）、盧基烏斯·埃米利烏斯·斯庫魯斯與昆圖斯·盧塔提烏斯·卡圖盧斯（前101年維爾凱萊的雙將軍）。辛布里方面的最高人物是「王」鮑伊奧里克斯，聯盟中最硬的骨頭是最後被消滅的條古里尼人。戰後的羅馬則把辛布里當成政治籌碼：西塞羅在演說裡反覆拿它嚇人，凱撒《高盧戰記》把它寫成全書的序幕，維吉利烏斯·費洛還寫了一部同名史詩。
peopleEn: The decisive figures on the Roman side were consuls and generals. The consuls of 113 BC, Gnaeus Papirius Masco and Publius Cornelius Scipio Asina, took the field along the eastern foothills of the Alps; Masco was routed by the Cimbrian host, the first defeat the Roman Republic suffered at the hands of northern tribes in this war, and Asina was killed during the withdrawal. The man who turned the war around was Gaius Marius, consul five times between 107 and 101 BC, who took the title of conqueror of the Cimbri in 104 BC and was the only participant to fight it from beginning to end. He reorganised the cohort as the tactical unit of the infantry, tightened the pairing of the pilum with the gladius, imposed stricter camp discipline, gave the cavalry an independent command, and folded Rhodian and Massaliot mercenaries and Gallic allies into the order of battle. In 105 BC he destroyed the Teutones at Aquae Sextiae with an ambush on the flank; from 104 BC he ground the Cimbri down with a long siege in the Po valley. Among his colleagues and subordinates were Marcus Junius Silanus, who was badly beaten at the Tagai in 109 BC; Quintus Servilius Caepio and Gaius Flavius Fimbria, whose army was wiped out at Arausio in 105 BC; and Lucius Aemilius Scaurus and Quintus Lutatius Catulus, the pair who won at Vercellae in 101 BC. On the Cimbrian side the highest figure was the king Boiorix, and the hardest core of the confederation was the Tigurini, the last to be destroyed. After the war Rome turned the Cimbri into a political instrument: Cicero used them repeatedly as a term of fear in his speeches, Caesar set them in the prologue of the Gallic War, and Vergilius Flaccus wrote an epic of the same name.
kits: 卡面是科林斯青銅盔：全正面開眼、只在鼻樑與眼孔之間留空隙的希臘式青銅頭盔，流行於公元前七世紀中葉，後來被伊利里亞式與色雷斯式頭盔取代，到本役開打時早已退到博物館裡；前線上真正戴的是馬薩利亞與羅得島雇傭兵的伊利里亞式頭盔，以及羅馬軍常見的蒙蒂式帽盔。所以這件兵器在辛布里戰爭裡的真正位置是對照件：它標示出這場戰爭跟希臘世界的接口，也提醒人青銅盔的代價——開闊的視野要靠隊形補償，視野越開闊，散兵線越致命。同期真正戴在頭上的是辛布里人自己的青銅頭盔：羅馬尼亞丘梅什蒂出土的這批辛布里頭盔帶鳥喙形面甲、巨大冠飾與獸形飾件，外形常被拿來與希臘—伊利里亞系統對照；辛布里步兵其餘裝備是長身鐵劍、橢圓形木盾與短投矛。羅馬這邊的標準組合是橢圓弧面大盾、短劍、重標槍與近身刺槍，輔以皮札甲、鍋盔與野外營壘，騎兵用長刀與投槍，野戰裡並沒有可以倚仗的投射砲兵，火力全落在標槍與弓箭上。還有兩件不該漏掉的東西：前113年羅馬唯一一次在歐洲戰役中使用戰象，以及馬略給全軍換上的羊頭徽記，那是他硬幣上的辛布里頭盔圖案，也是「以辛布里為名」的正式榮譽。最後是辛布里人的車隊，那種被敵人視為戰利品的大篷車，與其說是行李，不如說是他們的移動堡壘。
kitsEn: The card shows a Corinthian helmet: a Greek bronze helmet with the full face open, leaving only a gap for the nose and the eyes. It was fashionable in the middle of the seventh century BC, was later displaced by Illyrian and Thracian types, and by the time this war was fought it belonged in a museum; the helmets actually worn on the line were the Illyrian type of the Massaliot and Rhodian mercenaries and the Montefortino-style cap of the Roman infantry. The weapon's real place in the Cimbrian War is therefore as a reference piece: it marks the interface between this war and the Greek world, and it drives home the price of a bronze helmet — the wide view has to be paid for by the formation, and the wider the view, the more fatal a broken line. What was genuinely worn on the head at the time were the Cimbri's own bronze helmets: the Cimbrian type excavated at Ciumești in Romania, with a bird's-beak visor, a large crest and animal-shaped fittings, is often compared with the Greek-Illyrian system. The rest of the Cimbrian infantry equipment was a long iron sword, an oval wooden shield and short throwing spears. The Roman side's standard combination was the curved oval scutum, the gladius, the heavy pilum and the thrusting hasta, supported by leather and scale armour, cap helmets and the field camp, with cavalry armed with long swords and javelins. There was no field artillery to rely on, so all firepower rested on the pilum and the bow. Two items must not be left out: the elephants, the only time Rome used war elephants in a European battle, in 113 BC, and the goat's-head emblem Marius gave the army, the Cimbrian helmet device on his coinage and the formal honour of bearing the Cimbrian name. Last of all stand the Cimbrian wagons, the great covered vehicles the enemy counted as booty, less a baggage train than a moving fortress.
tactics: 波里比俄斯留下的戰術描寫，是這場戰爭最珍貴的技術資料。前113年諾里西姆谷地一役，辛布里人沒有擺出希臘式的密集方陣，而是散開成流動隊形，像洪流一樣沿谷地與山壁湧下，邊走邊唱戰歌、吶喊；他們用馬隊包抄，以長身鐵劍砍斷羅馬人仍插在盾上的標槍，再順勢劈開盾牌與手臂。羅馬人把戰象與騎兵擺在前面、步兵列成長線，結果前鋒被沖散，受驚的象群衝亂自己的步兵，羅馬全軍大潰；只有羅得島標槍中隊在後方結陣，勉強接住潰兵。馬略的做法是把「不讓敵人決定交戰時間與地形」寫進制度：前105年阿奎·塞克斯提亞，他讓強敵從營地前經過，等他們走到平地、縱隊拉長、陣形打散，才以兩翼騎兵與步兵同時發動側擊；前101年維爾凱萊，羅馬人先用步兵假退，把辛布里人引出營地，誘其把追兵與輜重丟下，等其側翼暴露，羅馬騎兵再一擊衝散其步兵陣。辛布里人自己也有紀律上的弱點：追擊時常為掠奪羅馬營地而中斷，讓追兵重新整隊；他們的營地與車隊成了羅馬最有效的目標。守方則靠羅馬營壘的木柵與壕溝，以及圍城戰術把高盧與利古里亞的城邑逐個拔除。整體看，這是一場以陣形對散兵線、以速度對重裝備的戰爭。
tacticsEn: The tactical description left by Polybius is the most valuable technical record of this war. At Noreia in 113 BC the Cimbri did not form a Greek-style tight phalanx: they spread into a fluid formation and poured down the valley and along the mountain flank like a torrent, singing a war song and shouting as they came, using their mounted men to envelop, and cutting down the Roman javelins that were still standing in the shields before hewing at shields and arms with their long swords. The Romans put elephants and cavalry in front with the infantry drawn out in a long line; the forward ranks were scattered, the frightened elephants broke the Roman infantry, and the whole army collapsed. Only the Rhodian cohort of javelin-throwers, formed up in the rear, caught the routed men. Marius's approach was to write into doctrine the rule that the enemy must not be allowed to choose the time and the ground: in 105 BC at Aquae Sextiae he let the strong enemy column march past his camp, waited until they were on the flat with their column stretched and their formation broken, and then struck the flanks with cavalry and infantry at the same moment; in 101 BC at Vercellae the Romans staged a retreat with the infantry to draw the Cimbri out of their camp and lure them into leaving the baggage behind, and when their flank was exposed the Roman cavalry charged and scattered the Cimbrian foot. The Cimbri had a discipline of their own to lose: they repeatedly broke off pursuit to plunder the Roman camp, letting the pursuers reform, and their camp and wagon train became the most profitable Roman target. On the defensive side Rome relied on the palisade and ditch of the marching camp and on siege operations that took the towns of Gaul and Liguria one by one. Taken as a whole, this was a war of formation against loose line, of speed against heavy equipment.
data: 留下數字的地方集中在兩處：一是波里比俄斯對前113年的記錄，二是前101年之後的戰果總帳。兵員方面，前113年兩位執政官各率步兵三萬、騎兵三千，合計約九十個步兵中隊與六千騎兵，另有羅得島標槍中隊一營；同一支大軍還帶著象群。辛布里一方沒有留下可用的數字，波里比俄斯只說其不可勝計，並描述了隨軍的牲畜、奴隸與數千輛車；學界對這個遷徙聯盟的常見估算落在數萬人的量級，但那只是量級，不能當作本役的實數。戰果方面，後世羅馬作家引述前101年維爾凱萊之役的數字為辛布里人陣亡一萬五千、被俘三萬；狄奧多羅斯記載前105年阿奎·塞克斯提亞的戰利品，說被俘者達數萬並被變賣，另有十餘萬頭牲畜以及大批青銅頭盔與盾牌被帶走。時間上，這場戰爭從前113年打到前101年，足足十二年，中間有四場羅馬全軍覆沒的大敗：前113年諾里西姆、前109年塔高、前105年阿勞西奧，以及前104年至前102年的拉烏迪納原野追擊戰。地理上，戰線自諾里西姆（今奧地利薩爾斯堡一帶）沿波河下游向東，直抵比斯開灣北岸的利古里亞，距離以百公里計，羅馬方面的補給靠海運與沿途築城維持，辛布里人則靠牛群與車隊隨行。損失記錄極少，數字幾乎都由勝方單方面記下。
dataEn: Numbers survive in only two places: Polybius' account of 113 BC, and the tallies of results written down after 101 BC. On strength, in 113 BC the two consuls each led about thirty thousand foot and three thousand horse, some ninety cohorts of infantry and six thousand cavalry in all, together with one cohort of Rhodian javelin-throwers, and the same army had elephants in its train. No usable figure survives for the Cimbri: Polybius simply calls their host beyond counting, describing the cattle, the enslaved followers and the thousands of wagons that came with it; the usual scholarly estimate for such a migrating confederation is on the order of tens of thousands, but that is an order of magnitude and not a return for this battle. On results, later Roman writers give for Vercellae in 101 BC the figures of fifteen thousand Cimbri killed and thirty thousand taken prisoner, while Diodorus, writing of the booty at Aquae Sextiae in 105 BC, says that the captives numbered many tens of thousands and were sold into slavery, and that more than a hundred thousand head of cattle and great quantities of bronze helmets and shields were carried off. In time, the war ran from 113 to 101 BC, twelve years in all, with four occasions on which a Roman army was destroyed: Noreia in 113 BC, the Tagai in 109 BC, Arausio in 105 BC, and the pursuit after the Raudine plain between 104 and 102 BC. In geography, the front ran from Noricum, around Salzburg in modern Austria, down the lower Po and east to the Ligurian coast on the Bay of Biscay, a distance measured in hundreds of kilometres; Rome's supply line depended on sea transport and on fortresses built as it advanced, while the Cimbri carried their own provisions in cattle herds and wagon trains. Casualty figures are scarce and nearly all come from the victors.
cause: 打起來的原因有三層。最外層是遷徙：公元前二世紀末到前一世紀初，日耳曼半島與北歐的部落聯盟因人口、耕地與牲畜的壓力向南移動，這種移動在當時的歐洲並不罕見，前58年赫爾維蒂人的大遷徙是更著名的一例。辛布里人與條頓人、阿姆布里昂人一路南下，進入北意大利的波河平原，撞上羅馬在阿爾卑斯東麓與高盧的邊界。第二層是羅馬自己造成的：羅馬在山南高盧設行省、在諾里西姆一線設防衛，等於擋在遷徙路徑上；而約前112年接納了被打敗的阿洛布羅吉人與阿維爾尼人進入羅馬境內避難，於是辛布里人的追擊順理成章地壓到羅馬邊界。第三層是外交失敗：阿洛布羅吉人與艾杜伊人先後派使團到羅馬求援，艾杜伊人自稱是羅馬人民的朋友與盟友，請求出兵；羅馬議會與執政官幾度拖延議事，前113年才倉促派兵，結果在諾里西姆一戰被迎頭擊潰。被打之後羅馬才把戰爭升級為全面對抗：先拒絕辛布里人的和談與歸還掠奪物的要求，再用十二年時間把這場邊境衝突變成一場消滅整個部族聯盟的戰爭。
causeEn: There were three layers of cause. The outermost was migration: from the late second and early first century BC, tribal confederations in the Jutland and northern European regions moved south under pressure of population, farmland and cattle, and such movement was not unusual in the Europe of the day, the great migration of the Helvetii in 58 BC being the better known case. The Cimbri, with the Teutones and Ambrones, came south, entered the Po valley of northern Italy, and ran into the Roman frontier in the eastern Alps and in Gaul. The second layer was Rome's own doing: Rome's province in Transalpine Gaul and its defensive line in Noricum stood directly across the path of that migration; and when the defeated Allobroges and Arverni were admitted around 112 BC to take refuge inside Roman territory, the Cimbrian pursuit of them pressed naturally up to the Roman border. The third layer was the failure of diplomacy: the Allobroges and then the Aedui sent embassies to Rome asking for help, the Aedui presenting themselves as the friends and allies of the Roman people, while the senate and the consuls debated at length and only dispatched an army in 113 BC, and that army was met head-on and destroyed at Noreia. Only after that defeat did Rome escalate the war into a general confrontation: the Cimbrian offers of peace and the return of plunder were refused, and the border conflict was turned over twelve years into a war aimed at the destruction of the whole tribal confederation.
impact: 這場戰爭的後果，一半在戰場之外。軍隊層面，羅馬自馬略時代起把步兵的基本作戰單位由百人隊改為中隊，並確立標槍洗臉、短劍收割的標準戰法；營壘的嚴格紀律、騎兵的獨立指揮與混合編成的輔兵制度，都因這十二年而改頭換面。政治層面，馬略在戰後以征服辛布里的名號與退伍軍人安置問題成為黨爭焦點；辛布里人後來在羅馬政治語言裡變成一個固定詞，辛布里即等於外來蠻族的恐怖。前五十年後，羅馬的邊界從阿爾卑斯退到萊茵，整個高盧被納入行省體系，辛布里戰爭正是這條擴張線的起點。希臘與拉丁的知識界也得到一批素材：波里比俄斯《歷史》第十卷是研究這場戰爭的主要文本，維吉利烏斯·費洛的史詩《辛布里戰爭》如今只剩片段；辛布里究竟指日耳曼人還是凱爾特人，從十八世紀到今天一直是考古與語言學界爭論不休的課題。而戰利品中的青銅頭盔、劍與盾被熔進羅馬的國庫，也說明這場戰爭最終贏的不是部族，是制度。
impactEn: Half the consequences of this war lie off the battlefield. At the level of the army, Rome moved from the maniple to the cohort as the basic tactical unit of the infantry, and fixed the standard sequence of the pilum followed by the gladius; the strict discipline of the camp, the independent command of the cavalry and the system of mixed auxiliary formations were all reshaped by these twelve years. At the political level, Marius found himself at the centre of factional conflict with his title of conqueror of the Cimbri and the question of settling his veterans; and the Cimbri entered Roman political language as a fixed term, Cimbri standing for the terror of the foreign horde. Later in the first century BC the Roman frontier moved back from the Alps to the Rhine and the whole of Gaul was drawn into the provincial system; the Cimbrian War is the starting point of that line of expansion. The Greek and Latin literary world received a body of material as well: Book 10 of Polybius is the principal text for the war, while Vergilius Flaccus' epic on the Cimbrian War survives only in fragments, and whether the Cimbri were Germans or Celts has been an argument among archaeologists and philologists from the eighteenth century to the present. The bronze helmets, swords and shields taken as booty were melted into the Roman treasury, which is another way of saying that what finally won this war was not a tribe but an institution.
result: 結局是辛布里聯盟的徹底崩解。前105年，條頓人在阿奎·塞克斯提亞被馬略全殲，數萬人被俘並被變賣為奴；同一年，辛布里人與阿姆布里昂人在阿勞西奧擊潰羅馬兩位將軍的大軍，殘部退往比斯開灣。前102年，馬略麾下的騎兵在拉烏迪納原野一役擊散辛布里人，迫使他們退入利古里亞並與利古里人合流，戰線延到熱那亞海岸；前101年，卡圖盧斯與斯庫魯斯在維爾凱萊以假退誘敵、騎兵側擊的辦法把辛布里主力打崩，陣亡與被俘的數字都以萬計。殘餘的條古里尼人退入日耳曼腹地，據說投奔卡蒂人，隨即被卡蒂人消滅，這是這場戰爭在戰鬥序列上的最後一筆帳；辛布里人自己的族中長老多有自焚以避降者。留下的名號是「辛布里之俘」與羊頭徽記。從羅馬的角度，這場戰爭是贏了：外來聯盟被逐出高盧，羅馬沒有滅掉一個國家，卻換來十二年實戰鍛出來的軍制，以及一道從阿爾卑斯通往萊茵的新邊界。
resultEn: The outcome was the complete disintegration of the Cimbrian confederation. In 105 BC the Teutones were annihilated by Marius at Aquae Sextiae, with tens of thousands captured and sold into slavery; in the same year the Cimbri and Ambrones destroyed the army of two Roman generals at Arausio and the remnants fell back toward the Bay of Biscay. In 102 BC the cavalry under Marius scattered the Cimbri in the fighting that followed the Raudine plain, driving them into Liguria, where they joined the Ligurians and carried the war to the coast at Genoa; in 101 BC Catulus and Scaurus broke the Cimbrian main force at Vercellae by staging a retreat and then charging the exposed flank with cavalry, and the numbers killed and captured ran into the tens of thousands. The surviving Tigurini withdrew into the depths of Germania, are said to have taken refuge with the Chatti, and were then destroyed by the Chatti; that was the last entry in the military ledger of this war, and among the Cimbri themselves several elders burned themselves rather than be taken. What remained behind were names: Capio Cimbrica, the one who took the Cimbrian name, and the goat's-head emblem. From the Roman point of view the war was won. The invading confederation was driven out of Gaul, Rome had not destroyed a state, and in exchange it received a military system forged in twelve years of fighting and a new frontier running from the Alps towards the Rhine.
